index.metaDescription: Short answers to common pallet questions: heat treatment, grades, weight, height, trailer fit, and pool ownership, each with one table, diagram, or calculator preset.

items.question: What does HT mean on a pallet?
items.summary: HT means the wood was heat treated to the ISPM 15 core temperature and time, then marked in the bordered stamp.
items.directAnswer: HT means heat treated. Under ISPM 15, the wood was heated until the core reached at least 56 °C (133 °F) for 30 continuous minutes, then marked by a licensed facility. Those letters sit in the bordered stamp with the IPPC symbol and the producer number. The [heat-treated pallets guide](/resources/heat-treated-pallets-ispm-15/) explains the full mark.

asset.heading: Stamp fields, annotated
asset.lead: The drawing is a schematic of the fields the heat-treated pallets guide lists. It is not a photograph of a stamp, and US-1234 is that guide's example, not a licensed facility.

callouts.label: Border
callouts.text: The mark sits inside a border. It has to be legible and permanent, and it is not hand-drawn.

callouts.label: IPPC symbol
callouts.text: A stylized wheat ear on the left. The mark here is a schematic, not the official logo.

callouts.label: Country code and producer number
callouts.text: Joined by a hyphen, as in US-1234. APHIS and U.S. Customs and Border Protection resumed enforcing that hyphen on January 1, 2026.

callouts.label: Treatment code
callouts.text: HT on this example. The same position can read DH, MB, or SF.

callouts.label: DUN
callouts.text: Added when the marked wood is dunnage rather than a pallet, crate, or box. A pallet mark does not need it.

items.question: Do I need heat-treated pallets for domestic shipping?
items.summary: A shipment that stays inside the United States does not need an ISPM 15 heat-treatment stamp.
items.directAnswer: No. ISPM 15 applies when wood packaging crosses a border, so a shipment that stays inside the United States does not need a heat-treatment stamp. Buyers still specify one when a plant also ships export orders, when a receiver asks for a stamp, or to limit insects between sites. See the [heat-treated pallets guide](/resources/heat-treated-pallets-ispm-15/).

asset.heading: When a domestic load still specifies HT
asset.lead: ISPM 15 is a border rule. The table applies it to situations the heat-treated pallets guide already names. It does not add a domestic legal requirement.

items.question: What is the difference between Grade A and Grade B pallets?
items.summary: Grade A and Grade B are trade labels for repair level and stringer condition, not a published standard.
items.directAnswer: In common trade usage, Grade A means structurally sound, with minimal repairs and no plated or doubled stringers. Grade B means sound but repaired, often with plated or companion stringers and mixed board widths. Neither label is a published standard, so confirm the written criteria. The [GMA pallets and grades guide](/resources/gma-pallets-and-grades/) is the reference.

items.question: How much does a standard 48 × 40 wood pallet weigh?
items.summary: Published figures for a 48 × 40 wood stringer pallet commonly run about 33–48 lb.
items.directAnswer: Published figures for a 48 × 40 wood stringer pallet commonly run about 33–48 lb, and a figure near 37 lb is often cited. Species, moisture, and board count move the number. The preset below is the weight estimator example, not a measured AGL weight. See the [weight and load capacity guide](/resources/pallet-weight-and-load-capacity/).

items.question: How much weight can a pallet hold?
items.summary: How much a pallet can hold depends on whether it sits on the floor, a forklift, or rack beams.
items.directAnswer: Capacity depends on support. A pallet on a solid floor carries the most, a pallet on a moving forklift carries less, and a pallet on rack beams usually carries the least. A published rating belongs to one design under stated conditions. The diagram shows the three cases. See the [weight and load capacity guide](/resources/pallet-weight-and-load-capacity/).

asset.heading: Static, dynamic, and racked
asset.lead: The three drawings match the three support conditions in the weight guide. They show where the pallet is supported. They do not assign a pound rating. Published ratings, including the figures CHEP and PECO state for their own block pallets, stay on the [weight and load capacity guide](/resources/pallet-weight-and-load-capacity/).

items.question: What is the standard pallet height?
items.summary: Most wood pallets fall around 5 to 6.5 inches, and a 48 × 40 is often described as about 6 inches tall.
items.directAnswer: There is no single standard pallet height. Most wood pallets fall around 5 to 6.5 inches, and a 48 × 40 wood pallet is often described as about 6 inches tall. Height is the decks plus the stringer or block, and it changes how many loads fit in a trailer. See the [pallet sizes guide](/resources/pallet-sizes/).

items.question: How many pallets fit on a 53 ft trailer?
items.summary: A 53 ft dry van takes 26 of the 48 × 40 pallets loaded straight or 30 turned, single-stacked.
items.directAnswer: For 48 × 40 pallets, single-stacked, a 53 ft dry van takes 26 loaded straight or 30 turned on the calculator's interior assumptions. Weight, product height, and receiver rules can cut that before the floor is full. The presets below are planning estimates, not a load plan. See [pallets per truckload](/resources/pallets-per-truckload/).

asset.heading: Calculator preset: straight and turned
asset.lead: Both presets use the truckload calculator's 53 ft dry van and its example loaded unit. Straight means the 48-inch side runs along the trailer. Turned means the 40-inch side does. These are planning estimates, not a carrier load plan. The form is on [pallets per truckload](/resources/pallets-per-truckload/#calculator).

items.question: How many pallets fit in a 40 ft container?
items.summary: The calculator's best simple pattern puts 20 of the 48 × 40 pallets on the floor of a standard 40 ft container.
items.directAnswer: A standard 40 ft ISO container is narrower than a dry van, so 48 × 40 pallets do not sit two across when turned. The calculator's best simple pattern for that interior is 20 pallets, single-stacked, on the example unit load. It is a planning estimate. See [pallets per truckload](/resources/pallets-per-truckload/).

asset.heading: Calculator preset: 40 ft standard container
asset.lead: This preset is the truckload calculator on the 40 ft standard ISO container, with the same example unit load. All-straight and all-turned floor counts sit beside the best simple pattern. It is a planning estimate. Open that equipment on the [pallets per truckload calculator](/resources/pallets-per-truckload/?eq=iso40#truckload-results).

items.question: How many empty pallets fit on a truckload?
items.summary: On the shared planning default, a turned 53 ft dry van holds about 510 empty 48 × 40 pallets.
items.directAnswer: Empty 48 × 40 wood pallets ship in stacks. On the shared planning default of 6 inches and 37 lb, the calculator's empty mode for a 53 ft dry van comes to about 510 pallets when turned. Space usually limits that load before weight does. See [pallets per truckload](/resources/pallets-per-truckload/).

asset.lead: Empty mode stacks the shared planning default, 6 inches and 37 lb, on the 53 ft dry van. The count below is the calculator's result, not a tally of a loaded truck. items.question: How many boxes fit on a pallet?
items.summary: The boxes calculator's example carton comes to 50 cartons on a 48 × 40 pallet.
items.directAnswer: Boxes per pallet is cartons per layer times the layers that fit under the height limit, column-stacked, with no overhang. The example preset is 50 cartons on a 48 × 40 pallet, not a measured pack. Enter your own carton to replace it. See the [pallet calculators guide](/resources/pallet-calculators/).

asset.lead: The preset is the boxes calculator's example: a 16 × 12 × 10 inch carton on a 48 × 40 pallet, 6 inches tall, under a 60-inch load height. It is an example, not a measured pack-out. Enter your carton on the [boxes per pallet calculator](/resources/pallet-calculators/boxes-per-pallet/).

items.question: What is a four-way pallet?
items.summary: A four-way pallet lets a forklift enter from all four sides, and true four-way also lets a pallet jack.
items.directAnswer: A four-way pallet lets a forklift enter from all four sides. On a notched stringer pallet, called partial four-way, a pallet jack still enters only the two ends. On a block pallet, called true four-way, jacks enter every side. The diagram shows both. See [types of pallets](/resources/types-of-pallets/).

asset.heading: Entry from the ends and the sides
asset.lead: Forklift entry and pallet-jack entry are not the same thing. The drawings use the entry types from the types of pallets guide. Notches let a forklift in from the side; a pallet jack still needs an opening in the bottom deck.

panels.title: True four-way
panels.how: Blocks, with openings for jack wheels

asset.note: A partial four-way pallet is four-way for a forklift and two-way for a pallet jack. True four-way needs the bottom deck to leave wheel openings.

items.question: Can you buy CHEP or PECO pallets?
items.summary: CHEP and PECO state that they keep ownership of their pallets and do not sell them.
items.directAnswer: No. CHEP states that it owns its pallets and never sells or otherwise gives up ownership. PECO states that its red block pallets are its property and may not be sold or bought. Pooled pallets at a dock go back through the pool pickup process. See [pooled vs. owned pallets](/resources/pooled-vs-owned-pallets/).

items.question: Is the ISO square pallet 1140 × 1140 or 1165 × 1165 mm?
items.summary: CHEP and many summaries say 1165 × 1165 mm, while other references list 1140 × 1140 mm for ISO 6780.
items.directAnswer: Sources disagree, and this library does not pick one. CHEP's Australian standard pallet is 1165 × 1165 mm, and many summaries call that the ISO square size. Other references list 1140 × 1140 mm for ISO 6780. The two do not match in a tight container. See the [pallet sizes guide](/resources/pallet-sizes/).
